title: Token-2022 extension risk matrix for integrators

environment.probe_source: crates/extensionlab-core/tests/extension_probe.rs (ported 2026-10-22); the first-run source is kept as research/logs/02_probe_litesvm-0.16.0_main.rs.txt

differences: CT.4: NonTransferable + ConfidentialTransferMint without ConfidentialMintBurn is accepted on 10.0.0 (11.0.0: InvalidExtensionCombination 0x33).
PB.1: PermissionedBurn does not exist on 10.0.0; its initializer (instruction 46) fails with InvalidInstruction 0xc (11.0.0: mint created).
not_probed_checks: PB.2 (standard BurnChecked on a PermissionedBurn mint)

evidence_tags.probe: executed in the LiteSVM probe and observed
evidence_tags.src: read in Token-2022 source, not executed
evidence_tags.doc: stated in official docs (solana-program.com or solana.com), not executed
evidence_tags.secondary: stated by a third-party security write-up, not executed
evidence_tags.unverified: our inference or expectation, not checked

severity_scale.high: a third party can move, destroy or indefinitely lock custodied tokens, or protocol accounting silently diverges from the vault balance
severity_scale.med: a standard flow reverts and is fixable in protocol code, or adds a liveness dependency on a user or issuer action, or amount math is wrong when UI amounts are used
severity_scale.low: fails loudly at listing or setup, or is cosmetic for custody flows

extensions.name: TransferFeeConfig
extensions.summary: Mint charges a fee in basis points, capped at maximum_fee, on every transfer; the fee is withheld in the destination account.
mutable_by: transfer_fee_config_authority (SetTransferFee; new fee applies at epoch + 2)

breaks.failure_mode: Protocol credits the instruction amount; vault receives amount minus fee (10000 deposited at 100 bps: vault 9900, withheld 100).
Paying out the credited amount exceeds the vault balance; the last withdrawer fails.
Round trip pays the fee twice (10000 -> 9900 in vault -> 9801 to user; 99 withheld on the user's account).

Fee is ceil(amount*bps/10000) capped at maximum_fee; amount 1 at 1% credits 0 and withholds 1. A fee change applies at epoch + 2 (credited 990, 990, 950 at epoch +0, +1, +2 after raising 100 to 500 bps).
A zero-balance vault with withheld fees cannot be closed until HarvestWithheldTokensToMint, which is permissionless.
Legacy Transfer (no mint) is rejected.
TransferCheckedWithFee with a stale or wrong expected fee is rejected.
A 165-byte token account cannot be initialized for this mint.

post_init: set_transfer_fee(bps, max) then advance Clock.epoch by 2 to make it effective
notes: Size token accounts with GetAccountDataSize, try_calculate_account_len with required extensions, or the ATA program.

actions: Credit the measured vault balance delta, or compute calculate_epoch_fee(current_epoch, amount).
Use transfer_checked_with_fee with the expected fee so fee changes fail fast.
Use calculate_inverse_epoch_fee when an exact net amount must arrive.
Harvest withheld fees before closing vaults.
Optionally reject mints whose current or newer fee exceeds a tolerance.
handling.detection: StateWithExtensions::<Mint>::unpack -> get_extension::<TransferFeeConfig>() -> get_epoch_fee(epoch), newer_transfer_fee.epoch, transfer_fee_config_authority (Some = mutable).

extensions.severity_note: Silent accounting insolvency in pooled vaults; blocked vault close.

extensions.name: TransferHook
extensions.summary: Token-2022 CPIs the mint's hook program (Execute) on every transfer_checked, after balances are updated.
mutable_by: transfer hook authority (Update program_id, including from None to Some)

breaks.failure_mode: CPI transfer that does not forward the hook program, validation PDA ["extra-account-metas", mint] and extra accounts fails.
Hook program id account passed but not an executable program.
Hook program passed with a missing or invalid validation account (probe used the memo program as a stand-in hook).
Hook authority switches the hook on after the protocol accepted the mint; a previously working transfer then fails.
Hook program can reject any transfer (blocklists, allowlists), reverting withdraw or refund.
Hook receives all transfer accounts read-only and without the sender's signer privilege.
Legacy Transfer (no mint) is rejected.
Self-transfers do not invoke the hook.

post_init: hook program's InitializeExtraAccountMetaList to create the validation PDA
notes: Realistic scenarios need real hook programs loaded with svm.add_program (always-allow, deny-all, deny-recipient, require-extra-writable-account). Not built in this task.

actions: Allowlist accepted hook program ids; reject others.
Reject mints whose hook authority is Some unless the issuer is trusted, or re-check program_id on every transfer.
In CPI, use spl_token_2022::onchain::invoke_transfer_checked and forward remaining accounts.
Clients resolve extra accounts off-chain (getTransferCheckedWithTransferHookInstructionAsync / createTransferCheckedWithTransferHookInstruction).
Prefer pull-based claims so one reverting transfer cannot block others (unverified design advice).

extensions.severity_note: Third-party code on every transfer can block withdrawals and refunds; can be switched on later.

extensions.name: PermanentDelegate
extensions.summary: A mint-level delegate can transfer or burn from any token account of the mint without the owner's signature; holders cannot revoke it.
mutable_by: current permanent delegate (SetAuthority PermanentDelegate; can reassign or set None)

breaks.failure_mode: Delegate transferred 600 and burned 400 from a PDA-style vault without the vault owner signing; vault balance 0.
Liabilities exceed vault balance after seizure; later withdrawals fail.
CPI Guard does not stop the permanent delegate.
Token-2022 logs 'Warning: Mint has a permanent delegate, so tokens in this account may be seized at any time' on InitializeAccount.

post_init: delegate signs transfer_checked or burn_checked as authority on any account
notes: Owner test a_permanent_delegate_moves_tokens_without_consent shows the same via CPI.

actions: Reject by default.
If a trusted issuer must be supported, reconcile liabilities against actual vault balance and define shortfall handling.

extensions.severity_note: Custodied tokens can be moved or destroyed without consent.

extensions.name: Pausable
extensions.summary: Pause authority can halt transfers, mints and burns for the mint.

breaks.failure_mode: transfer_checked while paused.
Refund or timeout logic cannot move tokens while paused; deadlines can be missed.
mint_to and burn_checked also fail while paused; Approve and closing an empty account still succeed.
Legacy Transfer (no mint) is rejected on PausableAccount accounts.

actions: Treat MintPaused as retryable.
Do not penalize users for deadlines missed during a pause.
Avoid partial state across multi-transaction flows.

extensions.severity_note: Issuer can lock custodied tokens indefinitely.

extensions.name: DefaultAccountState (Frozen)
extensions.summary: New token accounts start Frozen; only the freeze authority can thaw them.
mutable_by: freeze authority (UpdateDefaultAccountState; affects only accounts created afterwards)

breaks.failure_mode: Newly created vault is frozen; deposit transfer fails.
mint_to into a new frozen account fails; 'create vault and deposit' in one transaction reverts.
The required freeze authority can freeze the vault after deposits; withdraw fails.
Refund into a freshly created user account fails the same way.
Frozen default without a freeze authority is rejected at InitializeMint2.

actions: Check account.base.is_frozen() after creating a vault and return a clear error.
Document that the issuer must thaw protocol vaults, or reject the mint.

extensions.severity_note: Onboarding failure on its own; the implied freeze authority is a separate risk that classic SPL tokens share.

extensions.name: MemoTransfer (required memo)
extensions.summary: Incoming transfers to the account need a memo instruction immediately before the transfer (in CPI: the previous processed sibling instruction).
mutable_by: token account owner (enable/disable; can add the extension later via Reallocate)

breaks.failure_mode: User reallocates their own account (165 -> 171 bytes) and enables required memos; protocol withdraw to that user without a memo fails.
Same for refunds and batched payouts; one recipient can revert a batch.
Deposit into a memo-required vault without a memo, or with the memo after the transfer, fails; outgoing transfers need no memo.
In CPI, the program must CPI the memo program immediately before the transfer CPI.

ordered_instructions: system create_account(space=171) or reallocate(&[MemoTransfer]) on an existing account
post_init: memo instruction to MemoSq4gqABAXKb96qnH8TysNcWxMyWCqXgDLGmfcHr (no accounts, UTF-8 data) placed directly before the transfer
notes: LiteSVM 0.16.0 loads SPL Memo at Memo1UhkJRfHyvLMcVucJwxXeuD728EqVDDwQDxFMNo (spl_memo-1.0.0.so) and MemoSq4gqABAXKb96qnH8TysNcWxMyWCqXgDLGmfcHr (spl_memo-4.0.0.so) by default.

actions: CPI a memo immediately before every outbound transfer (always, or when memo_required(&destination)).
Do not enable required memos on protocol vaults.

extensions.severity_note: Recipient-controlled revert of payouts; easy to fix in code.

extensions.name: CpiGuard
extensions.summary: Owner-enabled account guard that blocks owner-signed transfer/burn, approve, close to a non-owner, and setting a close authority via CPI; owner change is always blocked.
mutable_by: token account owner (enable/disable at top level only; CpiGuardSettingsLocked 0x29 in CPI)

breaks.failure_mode: Standard deposit where the program CPIs transfer_checked with the user as authority.
Program CPIs Approve on the user's account.
Program closes the user's token account via CPI with lamports to a non-owner.
Program CPIs burn with the owner as authority.
SetAuthority(AccountOwner) fails even at top level while the guard is on; top-level transfer and approve succeed.

notes: The TLV entry exists only after enable_cpi_guard (extensions [] before, [CpiGuard] after).
CPI cases need the user's program, which ExtensionLab runs anyway; not executed in this probe.

actions: Support a delegate flow: user signs a top-level Approve, program transfers as delegate.
Or: user does a top-level transfer and the program verifies the vault balance delta.

extensions.severity_note: User-controlled revert of the most common deposit pattern; no custody loss.

extensions.name: MintCloseAuthority
extensions.summary: Close authority can close the mint when supply is 0; the address can then be re-initialized as a different mint.
mutable_by: close authority (CloseAccount on the mint; SetAuthority CloseMint)

breaks.failure_mode: Close with supply > 0 is rejected; with supply 0 the mint disappears while token accounts remain.
Mint re-created at the same address with different decimals (6 -> 0) and extensions (+10% fee); old zero-balance accounts accept mint_to under the new mint.
Vault created before resurrection lacks TransferFeeAmount; fee-bearing deposits into it fail.
Re-created mint with DefaultAccountState(Frozen): old accounts stay unfrozen and transfer without being thawed.
Re-created mint with a transfer hook: transfers out of old accounts fail.
Re-created NonTransferable mint: mint_to old accounts is blocked.

post_init: resurrect: create_account again with the same mint keypair and a different extension set

actions: Revalidate mint decimals and extension allowlist on every instruction instead of caching.
Check that vault account extensions still match the mint's required account extensions.
Optionally reject mints with a close authority; this alone is not sufficient because a re-created mint need not carry the extension (secondary source).
handling.detection: mint.get_extension::<MintCloseAuthority>() with close_authority.is_some(). Past resurrection is not visible from the current mint alone (unverified).

extensions.severity_note: Stale validation and stranded vaults; frozen-default bypass on resurrected mints.

extensions.name: InterestBearingConfig
extensions.summary: UI amount accrues continuously compounded interest from a basis-point rate; raw amounts never change and no tokens are created.

breaks.failure_mode: Raw balance 1000000000 (6 decimals) unchanged while UI amount went 1000 -> 1051.236557 after one simulated year at 5%.
UiAmountToAmount("1000") returned 951260678 raw after that year; storing or pricing in UI amounts drifts.
Rate authority set -1000 bps; UI amount then decreased.
Cannot be combined with ScaledUiAmount.

post_init: amount_to_ui_amount returns a UTF-8 string in return data

actions: Account in raw u64 only; convert to UI at the display edge.

extensions.severity_note: Low if the protocol never uses UI amounts.

extensions.name: ScaledUiAmount
extensions.summary: UI amount equals raw amount times the active multiplier; a new multiplier can be scheduled for a future timestamp.

breaks.failure_mode: Raw 1000000 unchanged; UI 1 before the scheduled time and 2 after; UiAmountToAmount("1") = 500000 after.
Reading only the stored multiplier field is wrong after new_multiplier_effective_timestamp; conversions use floating point and do not round-trip exactly.

actions: Use raw amounts and non-scaled prices for all calculations.
Round down when converting user UI input to raw.

extensions.severity_note: Low if the protocol never uses UI amounts.

extensions.name: NonTransferable
extensions.summary: Tokens cannot be transferred; owners can still burn and close.

breaks.failure_mode: Any transfer, including deposit, fails.
A 165-byte account cannot be initialized (needs 174).
mint_to an account lacking ImmutableOwner/NonTransferableAccount fails.

notes: NonTransferable + ConfidentialTransferMint without ConfidentialMintBurn fails InvalidExtensionCombination (probe). On 10.0.0 the combination is accepted and the mint is created (probe); the rule is in interface 3.1.1's check_for_invalid_mint_extension_combinations, not in 2.1.0 (src).

actions: Reject at listing; escrow requires transfers.

extensions.severity_note: Fails loudly on the first deposit.

extensions.name: ImmutableOwner
extensions.summary: Token account owner cannot be reassigned; the ATA program always adds it for Token-2022 accounts.

breaks.failure_mode: Escrow that reassigns an initializer's token account (or ATA) to a PDA with SetAuthority(AccountOwner) fails; the same call succeeds without the extension.

notes: Or create through the ATA program: data [0] Create, [1] CreateIdempotent. Token-2022 ATA extensions observed: [ImmutableOwner].

actions: Transfer into program-owned or PDA-owned vault accounts instead of reassigning ownership.

extensions.name: ConfidentialTransfer (and ConfidentialTransferFee)
extensions.summary: Encrypted balances and transfer amounts using ElGamal and ZK proofs; each account must be configured by its owner with a proof.
mutable_by: confidential transfer mint authority (approval policy, auditor key)
token account owner (configure, enable/disable confidential and non-confidential credits)

breaks.failure_mode: Recipient disabled non-confidential credits; public refund/payout to that account fails.
Account with non-zero confidential balance cannot be closed until EmptyAccount.
Confidential deposits land in an encrypted pending balance that needs the owner's keys to apply; a program-owned vault cannot use them without off-chain keys.
Attacker can exceed maximum_pending_balance_credit_counter on a configured account, blocking incoming confidential transfers.
ConfidentialTransferMint + TransferFeeConfig without ConfidentialTransferFeeConfig is rejected.
None on the public path: transfer_checked between unconfigured accounts works unchanged.

post_init: ConfigureAccount with a PubkeyValidity proof (instruction offset)
Deposit / ApplyPendingBalance / Transfer with equality, ciphertext-validity and range proofs in context-state accounts
notes: Full lifecycle exists in the owner's tests/confidential.rs; not re-run here.

actions: Support the public path only; never configure protocol vaults for confidential transfers.
Treat NonConfidentialTransfersDisabled on payouts as a per-recipient failure (prefer pull-based claims).

extensions.severity_note: Recipient-controlled payout failures; public path unchanged.

extensions.name: MetadataPointer / TokenMetadata
extensions.summary: Pointer to the account holding metadata (often the mint itself); TokenMetadata stores name/symbol/uri in the mint as a variable-length TLV.
mutable_by: metadata update authority (field updates; unverified, not probed)

breaks.failure_mode: Pointer to an arbitrary foreign address is accepted; mint and metadata must point to each other or identity can be spoofed.
Mint grows 234 -> 364 bytes on metadata init; Token-2022 reallocates but the account must already hold rent for the new size.
None: transfer_checked works unchanged.

ordered_instructions: spl_token_metadata_interface::instruction::initialize(program_id=Token-2022, metadata=mint, update_authority, mint, mint_authority, name, symbol, uri)
notes: Metadata TLV size = 4 + 32 + 32 + (4+name) + (4+symbol) + (4+uri) + 4 bytes (matched the observed 130-byte growth).

actions: Ignore for custody; identify tokens by mint address, never by metadata.

extensions.name: GroupPointer / TokenGroup / GroupMemberPointer / TokenGroupMember
extensions.summary: Collection configuration: group mints and member mints that point to them.

breaks.failure_mode: Group max_size enforced: third member with max_size 2 fails.
Group mint grows 234 -> 318 bytes on initialize_group; needs pre-funded rent.
None: process_transfer has no group checks.

ordered_instructions: group mint: create_account, group_pointer::instruction::initialize(authority, Some(mint)), initialize_mint2, spl_token_group_interface::instruction::initialize_group(program_id=Token-2022, group=mint, mint, mint_authority, update_authority, max_size)

member mint: create_account, group_member_pointer::instruction::initialize(authority, Some(mint)), initialize_mint2, initialize_member(Token-2022, member, member_mint, member_mint_authority, group, group_update_authority)
notes: Fund extra lamports for the post-init growth.

actions: Ignore for escrows.

extensions.name: PermissionedBurn
extensions.summary: Every burn needs the burn authority's co-signature; standard Burn and BurnChecked are rejected. Not in the original brief; included because it is in program v11.
mutable_by: permissioned burn authority (SetAuthority PermissionedBurn; None restores standard burns per docs)

breaks.failure_mode: Protocols that burn (redemption, burn-on-withdraw) using standard BurnChecked fail; the permissioned burn instruction with co-signature succeeds.

notes: On 10.0.0 the extension does not exist: its initializer (instruction 46) fails with InvalidInstruction 0xc, so no such mint can be created and the burn results were not re-run (probe). Interface 2.1.0 has no permissioned_burn module.

actions: Reject for burn-based designs; no change for pure escrows.

extensions.severity_note: Low for escrows; med for burn-based protocols.

cross_cutting.finding: Extension presence is not activity: hook program, fee rate, pause flag, default state, permanent delegate, rate and multiplier can change after a protocol accepts the mint. Detection must read the config and whether an authority exists.

PYUSD mint 2b1kV6DkPAnxd5ixfnxCpjxmKwqjjaYmCZfHsFu24GXo (mainnet, read 2026-10-21, slot ~459697278) carries PermanentDelegate (set), TransferFeeConfig (0 bps, authority set), TransferHook (program null, authority set), MintCloseAuthority (set), ConfidentialTransferMint, ConfidentialTransferFeeConfig, MetadataPointer, TokenMetadata and a freeze authority.

Mint extensions force account extensions at InitializeAccount; hardcoded 165-byte vaults fail with InvalidAccountData. GetAccountDataSize for a TransferFee+Pausable+TransferHook mint returned 187 (191 with ImmutableOwner); the ATA was 191 bytes.
Legacy Transfer fails with MintRequiredForTransfer (0x1f) on accounts with TransferFeeAmount, TransferHookAccount or PausableAccount.
Closed mints can be re-created at the same address with different config; old accounts keep working with surprising results (frozen-default bypass, stranded fee-less vaults).

Mint extensions (except TokenMetadata/TokenGroup/TokenGroupMember) must be initialized after create_account and before InitializeMint2; violations and unreserved/unused space fail with InvalidAccountData.

notes: Same on interface 2.1.0 for every type it has. PermissionedBurn is not in interface 2.1.0 or Token-2022 10.0.0.
